text: The data shows the owner removed trees after 2020, but whether they broke the law depends on local regulations. Between 2021 and 2023, tree-cover loss totaled **87.4 hectares** (2.4% of the asset), confirmed by independent datasets. Most losses (81.3 ha in 2021) matched JRC’s 2020 forest map, meeting the analysis’s corroboration rule. However, small patches (<0.5 ha) were excluded from "events," totaling 38.9 ha of additional loss. If local laws permit removal below a certain threshold or require permits (not checked here), the owner might have complied. The data alone can’t confirm illegality—legal review of applicable regulations is needed.
